The dataset flow spends real Bright Data credits (one Web Scraper collection) and waits 5 minutes for the snapshot; AfterAll timeout is 600 s. If a collection routinely needs longer, raise the Wait interval rather than the assert.

FindSnapshotRecords declares no schema-level required inputs on purpose: snapshotId feeds the component's own dynamic outPort source, and the e2e rule 'dynamic-source-static-input' rejects a required source input bound to a modifier. Two Bright Data doc pages contradict each other on the TriggerDatasetCollection request body ({"input": [...]} vs a plain array); the plain array was chosen from the official trigger page. UNVERIFIED — this is the most likely first-contact failure once the dataset chain is tested.
Bright Data publishes no single hard rate limit; quota.js uses a conservative 10 requests/second sliding window. Revisit once real 429 behaviour is observed.

RESOLVED 2026-08-25: the doc contradiction on the TriggerDatasetCollection body is moot — the API accepts BOTH shapes. A direct probe returned 200 with a snapshot_id for the plain array AND for {"input":[...]}. A deliberately malformed body returned 400 validation_error with per-field detail, confirming what a real payload rejection looks like. The connector sends the plain array and works.

The whole async dataset chain is verified end to end: trigger -> snapshotId -> GetSnapshotStatus ready -> FindSnapshotRecords returning real records. The snapshot became ready within seconds, not the 5 minutes the E2E flow waits for.

ScrapeUrl and FindSearchResults now fail with a precise 400 zone "<name>" not found, which proves the components build a correct request and the only thing missing is a provisioned zone. GET /status still reports can_make_requests:false / auth_fail_reason:zone_not_found — that flag governs the Web Unlocker and SERP proxy products ONLY; the Datasets API is unaffected by it, as the passing dataset chain shows.
